model_params.features: combined wave-9 feature set: the 10 time-domain statistics of the earlier waves (untouched) + 14 spectral/envelope features (platform_lib.features.spectral). All spectral quantities are RATE-FREE: frequencies and band edges are fractions of Nyquist (8 log-spaced bands over 0.005..1.0 x Nyquist), band energies are normalised by total spectral energy, and the envelope peak amplitude is normalised by total envelope-spectrum magnitude — so the identical feature definitions apply at CWRU's 12 kHz and Paderborn's 64 kHz. This removes the sampling-rate confound only; it does not align shaft-speed-relative defect frequencies across rigs.
model_params.training: fit on ALL cwru windows of the shared label set; no target data in training

split.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all cwru windows, tested on all paderborn windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']. Identical to the wave-5 transfer protocol — the ONLY change is the feature set (10 time-domain -> 24 combined).

preprocessing.feature_note: combined wave-9 feature set: the 10 time-domain statistics of the earlier waves (untouched) + 14 spectral/envelope features (platform_lib.features.spectral). All spectral quantities are RATE-FREE: frequencies and band edges are fractions of Nyquist (8 log-spaced bands over 0.005..1.0 x Nyquist), band energies are normalised by total spectral energy, and the envelope peak amplitude is normalised by total envelope-spectrum magnitude — so the identical feature definitions apply at CWRU's 12 kHz and Paderborn's 64 kHz. This removes the sampling-rate confound only; it does not align shaft-speed-relative defect frequencies across rigs.
preprocessing.windowing: non-overlapping 2048-sample windows in both datasets — the window TIME SPAN still differs by sampling rate: 2048 samples = 170.7 ms at CWRU's 12 kHz vs 32.0 ms at Paderborn's 64 kHz. The spectral features are computed per window in rate-free units, but a window on one rig still observes ~5.3x more shaft revolutions than on the other.
preprocessing.excluded: CWRU 'Ball' class excluded (Paderborn scope has no ball-fault bearing); CWRU windows of that class are dropped from BOTH training (when CWRU is the source) and scoring
preprocessing.scaling: none (tree model, as in the wave-5 records)

notes: Zero-shot cwru -> paderborn bearing-fault transfer with the wave-9 combined spectral feature set — the wave-5 transfer re-run with the feature set as the only changed variable. Shift factors that remain, documented rather than corrected: different test rigs, bearing geometries, sensor mounting and load/speed regimes; shaft-speed-relative defect frequencies are NOT aligned by the rate-free features (sampling rate and shaft speed vary independently); window time spans differ 5.3x. The wave-5 time-domain baseline for this direction is carried in extra.wave5_time_domain_baseline; the result is reported as measured, whether or not it improves.

reference_target_in_domain.protocol: MEASUREMENT-GROUPED split: GroupShuffleSplit by source_file (measurement id), 80/20, seed 42 — no measurement file contributes windows to both sides. NOTE: there is only ONE physical bearing per class
